ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, HMT sanctions, and applicable Vanuatu sanctions and terrorism-financing designations; mandatory identification of politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates, requiring enhanced due diligence (EDD) and senior management approval under the AML/CTF Act No. 13 of 2011 and VFSC guidance. All CDD and EDD records must be updated at least annually and preserved for a minimum of five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Company Registry - online name clearance and incorporation portal (www.vfsc.vu / e-VFSC filing system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be submitted in English or French using Latin characters; no indigenous transliteration is mandated. An International Company name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Societe Anonyme', or a recognized abbreviation thereof, and must not be identical or deceptive in relation to an existing registered name or imply royal or governmental sponsorship or any licensed activity absent the relevant license.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Vanuatu (where use implies official governmental affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the VFSC Registrar within 21 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds for review and attaching any ministerial consent or supporting authorization; the Registrar shall respond within 10 business days. If the objection is upheld, the applicant may request a 30-day extension of an existing reservation before expiry. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may either submit a new name clearance application or pursue judicial review before the Supreme Court of Vanuatu.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible solely for the statutory registered office of the International Company, which must be located at the premises of a licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu. However, an International Company is statutorily barred from carrying on business with persons resident in Vanuatu and from holding an interest in land in Vanuatu; accordingly, the physical specialty tea salon and dine-in lounge operations must be held and licensed through a separate domestic Vanuatu company under the Companies Act [Cap. 191], with the IC acting as the tax-exempt offshore IP, branding, and procurement holding vehicle.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: IC offshore holding layer: approximately 5% probability of direct VFSC on-site inspection within the first three years (regulatory inspections are focused on licensed registered agents); domestic operating tea lounge: approximately 90% probability of on-site inspection by the Municipal Council and/or health and fire authorities prior to issuance and renewal of the food and beverage establishment license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap. 222] (No. 32 of 1992, as amended), particularly ss. 5, 9 to 18, 22, and 115 read together with the International Companies Fees Regulations [Cap. 222].
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Private Mail Bag 12023, Port Vila, Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association with Statement of Capital, delivered for registration under section 9 of the International Companies Act and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Vanuatu International Company; the subscriber shares may be either nil-paid or fully-paid as stated in the Statement of Capital. No escrow deposit or capital control filing is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board unanimously RESOLVES, effective upon the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, that (i) each subscriber identified in the Statement of Capital do hereby subscribe to and accept the shares allotted, fully paid to the extent set out in the Articles; (ii) the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the address in Port Vila, Vanuatu designated by the registered agent, until lawfully changed by later resolution; (iii) the individuals named in the consent to act are appointed as first directors and company secretary of the Company; (iv) such officers and directors are authorised to execute all banking, licensing, and contractual instruments and to cause any statutory filings necessary under the International Companies Act to be completed within the prescribed periods.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and corporate structure screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry, operating through a VFSC-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed agent to submit a name clearance request to the VFSC Registry, together with a short corporate profile and beneficial-owner screening form, and obtain written approval of the reserved International Company name.
required_dossiers: Proposed International Company name (one primary and two alternatives)
Short corporate profile indicating intended business scope
Ultimate beneficial owner and subscriber screening information
Registered agent written consent to act for the proposed company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or conditionally reserved, the agent must resubmit up to three alternative names within one business day; a conditionally approved name may be accepted and the original name re-applied for after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of formation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed registered agent and a Vanuatu notary public or recognized foreign notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association, Statement of Capital, consent-to-act forms, and registered office notice. Each subscriber, director, and secretary must execute and notarize the documents; the agent then prepares the VFSC application file.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (original, dated)
Statement of Capital showing subscriber shares and aggregate nominal value
Consent to act as first director and company secretary
Certified passports and proof of residential address for each subscriber, director, and secretary
Declaration of compliance with lawful business restrictions in the International Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defective notarization or incomplete statement of capital must be cured by a supplementary notarial certificate before filing; the agent will prepare corrected execution pages and resubmit documents to the notary within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic lodgement of incorporation application and fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Registry – International Companies Section (official online portal and scheduled courier lodgement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent transmits the full incorporation file to the VFSC Registry, pays the prescribed government filing fee by bank transfer or VFSC approved electronic means, and obtains an acknowledgement with a unique application reference number.
required_dossiers: VFSC International Company incorporation application form (Form IC-001)
Certified executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notice of registered office within Vanuatu
Consent to act forms for first director and secretary
Proof of government filing fee payment
Registered agent due-diligence certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or deficiency letter, the registered agent must respond within 10 business days with a supplementary letter, corrected form, or additional due-diligence evidence; if unresolved, the applicant may request a 15-business-day extension or withdraw and refund any unapplied portion of the fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VFSC vetting and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar reviews the filed instruments for compliance with the International Companies Act and, upon satisfaction, executes and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The certificate, filed Memorandum and Articles, and initial register extracts are then returned to the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Complete VFSC incorporation file with application reference number
Government-fee receipt or electronic payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If formal compliance is not achieved, the company may file corrective Articles and a rectification declaration within 15 days; the Certificate may then be reissued with an as-of date, or the application can be re-filed as a fresh incorporation with a new name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, corporate kit, and statutory governance activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors and the VFSC-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the pro-forma board resolutions, issue share certificates, elect the designated registered office, appoint the initial officers, and authorize all operational banking and licensing actions. The agent issues the corporate seal, share certificates, statutory registers, and maintenance manual.
required_dossiers: Signed minutes of the first board meeting
Form of share certificates issued to subscriber shareholders
Registered office confirmation letter and address details
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and execution of commercial contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any missing corporate seal or incomplete meeting minute may be cured by a written circular resolution executed by all directors and retained in the statutory register; the registered agent will correct register entries and issue notarized extracted minutes on the same business day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Department – Business Licence Section, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, under the Business Licences Act [Cap. 244]
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence for Specialty Tea Salon and Cultural Ceramic Lounge (Retail and Beverage Service Classification 63.10/NAICS 722515, non-liquor, non-entertainment food and drink service)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change and Natural Resources, Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Certificate – Registration Category E3 (low-impact retail food and beverage service), Full EIA Report not required unless the premises discharge effluent to an environmentally sensitive receiving water body or generate significant waste heat/odor
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Vanuatu Waste Management and Pollution Control Act and DEPC guidance: wastewater pH 6.0–9.0, BOD5 not exceeding 50 mg/L, total suspended solids below 60 mg/L, and oil/grease below 10 mg/L; install grease traps and brown-water separation; solid waste must be segregated and removed by a licensed contractor; indoor ventilation must keep airborne particulate and VOCs within occupational exposure thresholds; no ozone-depleting refrigerants in HVAC equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Vanuatu Fire Services and Port Vila Municipal Council covering occupancy load, exit routes, extinguishers and evacuation plan; structural load inspection certificate from the Public Works Department confirming the salon floor load for display shelving and lounge furniture; and occupational health clearance from the Department of Health and Department of Labour under the Occupational Health and Safety Act covering safe food handling, staff hygiene and slip-resistance controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs (VRC), Department within the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; official portal https://vurc.gov.vu; customs processing via VRC Customs ASYCUDA World single window; entity incorporation registry is the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), with foreign investment clearance by the Vanuatu Foreign Investment Promotion Agency (VFIPA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] at VFSC and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and registered agent confirmation. 2) Obtain a Foreign Investment Certificate from VFIPA if any natural or juridical foreign investor holds a beneficial interest. 3) For non-offshore domestic activity (specialty tea salon), obtain a municipal Business Licence (Port Vila or Luganville Municipality) and, if foreign owned, apply for the standard local trading conversion procedure, because a pure IC cannot trade with Vanuatu residents. 4) Apply to VRC on VAT Form REG-01 for compulsory VAT registration once taxable turnover exceeds VT 10,000,000 in any 12-month period, or voluntarily below the threshold; VRC then issues the VAT Registration Certificate and VAT registration number, which functions as the de facto national TIN. 5) Register for customs importer/exporter code under the Customs Act 2004 and open an Authorised Dealer relationship with a licensed bank for exchange control approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, flow-through, or hybrid mismatch election exists under Vanuatu law. The IC automatically enjoys statutory tax exemption under s.104 of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] (exempt from income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty and estate duty) conditioned on the IC not carrying on business in Vanuatu and deriving no Vanuatu-sourced income; local trading activity (on-premise tea service) forfeits the exempt status and attracts VAT and municipal licensing obligations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT Act No. 2 of 1998, effective 1 August 1998, as amended) supplemented by Customs Duties under the Customs Act 2004 and municipal business licence fees; the IC remains in the Tax_Exempt_Zone for direct taxes but is fully exposed to VAT on domestic taxable supplies and on imported goods
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 10,000,000 (ten million Vatu) of taxable turnover in any 12-month period above which VAT registration is compulsory; voluntary registration is available below the threshold; a foreign IC whose only supplies are exported goods or offshore services is generally outside the VAT charge but must still register if it makes taxable domestic supplies (e.g., salon retail sales) exceeding the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Vanuatu has no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing API, or digital stamping mandate. Standard VAT invoice rules apply: consecutive serial number, date, supplier name and VAT number, recipient name, description of supply, tax-exclusive amount, VAT amount at 12.5%, and total. The tea salon's local POS and card rails must generate compliant VAT receipts; export transactions must be separately evidenced for zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under s.11 of the VAT Act, (i) a supply of goods is zero-rated when the goods are exported by the supplier and leave Vanuatu within 30 days of supply; and (ii) a supply of services is zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident for use wholly outside Vanuatu. For the specialty tea salon and lounge, zero-rating is available for (a) loose-leaf tea, ceramics, and merchandise sold as export consignments that physically leave Vanuatu within the 30-day rule, and (b) offshore consulting, wholesaling or cultural-service fees supplied to non-resident clients for use abroad. On-premise tea service, retail takeaway consumed in Vanuatu, and catering remain taxable at 12.5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged electronically via VRC Customs ASYCUDA World (approved exporter code required)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the tea salon goods from Vanuatu within 30 days of supply
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the goods, quantity, and zero-rated value
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice showing receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident purchaser
VAT zero-rating schedule and export register maintained and retained for VRC audit inspection
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VRC may audit export zero-rating claims and, where the 30-day export rule, documentary bundle, or offshore-use requirement is not satisfied, assess the uncollected 12.5% VAT as output tax together with penalty tax and monthly interest (penalty tax and interest apply per the VAT Act late-payment rules). Fraudulent zero-rating claims or false declarations constitute tax evasion under the VAT Act, exposing the IC, its registered agent, and its directors to criminal fine and imprisonment (up to 2 years) and to retrospective clawback of all improperly claimed refunds plus penalties. All supporting customs, banking, and sales records must be retained for at least 7 years to withstand a VRC audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), Port Vila
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu vatu (VUV) is freely convertible for current account transactions (trade in goods and services, freight, insurance, worker remittances) and capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, loan disbursements, portfolio-related transfers), with no mandatory prior RBV approval for payments made through an RBV-authorized dealer bank. Profit and dividend remittance require standard bank AML/KYC verification, tax-clearance evidence where applicable, and a Board resolution; no separate exchange-control permit, dividend block, or surrender threshold applies. However, the International Company (Cap 222) is tax-exempt and may not conduct on-island domestic commerce, so profit remittance from a physical specialty tea salon must run through the resident operating company's accounts rather than through the IC offshore treasury layer. Market depth is thin for VUV, and commercial banks determine effective convertibility of large or exotic currency pairs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio into VUV. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in an RBV-authorized dealer bank account. For the tea-salon cross-border trade, export proceeds from high-end loose-leaf tea and cultural ceramics should be reported to the commercial bank as export proceeds for BPM6 balance-of-payments statistics; shipping documentation, commercial invoices, customs entries, and evidence of delivery must be retained to verify the underlying trade and satisfy AML source-of-funds obligations. There is no statutory timeline for conversion or repatriation beyond standard bank record-keeping rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational VUV/USD/AUD account for domestic tea-salon revenue; Capital Escrow Account for import and LC collateral
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium - available to a resident operating subsidiary; Low for a pure International Company without domestic trading substance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency treasury account plus trade finance and FX facility for cross-border tea leaf and ceramic supplier payments
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: High - strongest trade finance desk; requires physical KYC and full beneficial-ownership register

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational merchant/business account with local POS and EFTPOS merchant acquiring; segregated account for prepaid tea subscriptions
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium/High - excellent for local POS and credit-card settlement; viable once the trading entity is converted to a resident domestic company

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational and Investment Escrow Account for inbound capital injection and future secured borrowing
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium - supports corporate accounts and treasury operations, but may require a stronger resident footprint

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low. Offshore digital EMI providers, including EU/UK e-money institutions and non-regulated international payment processors, are not licensed by the RBV, do not have direct access to the Vanuatu domestic clearing system, and cannot act as the acquiring bank for local POS or on-island credit-card terminals under RBV payment-system rules. Such providers may be used only as a secondary non-VUV supplier-payment tool after the primary on-island bank relationship is established; all Vanuatu-source retail revenue must be settled through a resident licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RBV AML/CFT regulations require licensed financial institutions to conduct full corporate and beneficial-owner due diligence before account activation. At least one director or authorized signatory with executive authority must attend a physical in-person interview at the bank's Vanuatu branch; remote-only onboarding is not generally available for an International Company. A resident operating company may be accepted with remote video verification only if proposed signatories are existing low-risk customers with clean regulatory and criminal records; such remote acceptance remains at the bank's sole discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt International Company with no local economic substance opening an on-island operating bank account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing under the International Companies Act Cap 222; proposed local substance plan and physical lease for the tea salon; VFSC trading-license application or licensed exempt-activity declaration; detailed business plan with projected sales, supplier universe, and POS locations; local employment roadmap; source of initial paid-in capital; certified Board resolutions naming all signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial-owner opacity through offshore holding companies or nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: Beneficial Ownership Register maintained in Vanuatu or the home jurisdiction; corporate organizational chart through to ultimate individual shareholders; notarized declarations of trust and nominee arrangements; passport copies, residential address proof, and professional references for each UBO; bank reference letters from existing banks; sworn source-of-wealth statement for any inbound injection exceeding VUV 10 million or equivalent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive specialty retail and possible false invoicing in premium loose-leaf tea and ceramic imports
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: executed supplier contracts with tea estates and ceramic kilns; pro-forma invoices, commercial invoices, and packing lists; bills of lading and airway bills; customs declarations and import duty payment records; phytosanitary, food-safety, and ceramic-glaze quality certifications; warehouse inbound/outbound records matching POS retail volumes; merchant-side raw transaction files for card-settlement reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained inbound third-party payments from group treasury into escrow or operational accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: intercompany loan agreement or equity subscription instrument; corporate charges register; Board resolution approving the capital or loan injection; source-of-funds evidence from the remitting bank, including transaction statement and bank reference; economic-purpose memorandum explaining the tea-salon expansion or refit; and proof that the remittance does not breach the International Company domestic trade prohibition.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate shareholder or group treasury bank to a beneficiary account held at an RBV-authorized dealer bank. Use BPM6-aligned purpose-code narrative 'Equity capital injection / direct investment in tea-salon operating entity' for a resident operating company, or 'Shareholder funding to International Company working capital account' for the offshore treasury account. The bank will require a deposit-attribution letter, Board resolution, certified subscription contract or loan agreement, and UBO declarations before posting the credit. For the planned on-island specialty tea salon, the inbound capital should be segregated in a Capital Escrow Account and released to the operating account only after the domestic trading company is incorporated and the statutory business license is obtained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use direct SWIFT MT103 cash-against-documents payments for recurring loose-leaf tea and ceramic inventory, supported by commercial invoice and packing-list evidence. For larger consignments, issue an Irrevocable Letter of Credit through the Vanuatu bank's trade desk using SWIFT MT700/MT707, and settle at maturity via banker's acceptance or SWIFT MT103. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A), open-account payments with trade credit insurance, and telegraphic transfers in VUV, USD, AUD, EUR, GBP, or CNY are permissible when effected through an RBV-authorized dealer bank. For card settlements, the on-island POS must be acquired by a licensed Vanuatu scheme member; cross-border offshore-acquiring for a physical storefront terminal is not permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Vanuatu Vatu (VUV) / USD and VUV / AUD forward contracts executed with an RBV-licensed commercial bank for documented trade or balance-sheet exposure
VUV / USD and VUV / AUD foreign-exchange swaps with RBV-authorized bank counterparties for short-term liquidity matching and repricing alignment
USD / VUV cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term capital refinancing hedging, subject to bank availability and RBV prudential reporting requirements
Trade-related forward purchases of USD, AUD, EUR, or GBP against documented import invoices for tea and ceramic inventory
Term-out interest-rate and FX packages on LC exposure offered by the licensed Vanuatu bank trade desk for confirmed supplier contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return - International Company (Form setting out registered office, registered agent, directors, shareholders, and share capital)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 1 month following the anniversary of the date of incorporation; annual government license fee payable on the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% per month or part thereof on the unpaid annual government fee; persistent default triggers VFSC notice, administrative strike-off, and dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License (Renewal) Fee for International Company based on authorized share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge per month of arrears; non-payment for 3 months permits the Registrar to strike the company off the Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (including details of any shareholding transfers and ultimate beneficial owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the incorporation anniversary date; event-driven updates of shareholding or control changes required within 14 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A civil penalty of up to 65,000 VUV and court-instigated remedial order for non-compliance; continued default may lead to registry flagging and strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Renewal Instruction (confirmation that the licensed local agent will continue to serve)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Vanuatu Registered Agent (private contract administered via VFSC-approved agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, effective on the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent resignation leads to loss of registered office in Vanuatu; failure to appoint a replacement within 30 days results in VFSC administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not applicable. Vanuatu International Companies are statutorily exempt from mandatory independent audit regardless of asset, revenue, or shareholder thresholds. Financial statements are not required to be filed with VFSC.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP acceptable for voluntary audit or internally prepared financial records; no Local GAAP filing requirement for International Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain and annually reconfirm a Beneficial Ownership Register with VFSC, identifying every individual with at least 10% direct or indirect shareholding, voting rights, or control. All shareholding transfers occurring during the year must be disclosed in the annual confirmation and notified to VFSC within 14 days of execution.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (statutory exemption); USD 1,500-3,000 if a voluntary independent review or audit is commissioned for banking or counterparty due diligence

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% - Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax. International Companies (ICs) registered under the International Companies Act (Cap. 222) are statutorily exempt from all taxes, duties, and statutory charges of Vanuatu, including corporate income tax, capital gains tax, and dividend tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate is 0%. No tax holiday is needed because the tax base is nil. A VFSC-issued Tax Exemption Certificate evidences the IC's unconditional exemption under ICA s. 6(1)-(2). Domestic Value Added Tax (12.5%) and Business License fees are irrelevant to an IC, provided it does not carry on business within Vanuatu.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return under the International Companies Act (Cap. 222), s. 219, submitted through the VFSC Online Registry Portal (agent-mediated e-filing). Where an Economic Substance filing is required, the Annual Economic Substance Return is lodged simultaneously through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return must be filed within one month following the anniversary of incorporation. The registered agent exclusively controls the filing timeline; directors and beneficial owners must provide updated KYC, shareholding, and officer data to the agent no later than 14 days before the anniversary deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered name, registration number, date of incorporation, and authorized share capital of the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners rely on the registered agent to transcribe data from the certificate of incorporation; no local tax ID is required. Names must match English-character registration records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Registered Agent and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, and licence number of the Vanuatu registered agent and the registered office address within Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent completes this section; non-resident clients may not change the registered office without written consent of the agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Class, number, and nominal value of issued shares; names and addresses of shareholders; names, addresses, and nationalities of directors and any secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders must supply certified passports, proof of residential address, and a banker's reference; bearer shares and nominee arrangements must be disclosed to the beneficial ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A solemn certificate executed by a director, secretary, or the registered agent confirming that the IC has complied with the International Companies Act during the preceding year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: False certification is a criminal offence. Non-resident directors should not delegate this certificate to persons who have no access to verifying the IC's actual activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration whether the IC carried on a 'relevant activity' (banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing/leasing, headquarters, holding, distribution/service, or intellectual property) in Vanuatu during the year; if none, a nil-activity statement is lodged.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a specialty tea salon operating physically outside Vanuatu, a nil-activity declaration is appropriate only if the Vanuatu IC performs no substantive operational functions. If the IC merely holds the foreign tea-salon operating subsidiary, the passive holding exemption applies and must be claimed explicitly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Financial Solvency and Audit Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the IC has maintained adequate financial records for at least 5 years and whether the directors claim an exemption from audit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must ensure the underlying tea-salon accounts are consolidated or retained at the registered office; the IC must retain records sufficient to reconstruct transactions, assets, and profit repatriation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly late-filing surcharge equal to 10% of the annual government fee for each month or part thereof. Continued default authorises the VFSC to strike the IC off the register, causing automatic dissolution, loss of legal capacity, and the freezing of bank assets. Reinstatement requires a court order, payment of all arrears and penalties, and a new agent's compliance certificate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Vanuatu does not impose withholding tax on dividends declared, paid, or distributed by an International Company. ICA s. 6(1)-(2) expressly exempts distributions, and there are no exchange controls or dividends-tax reporting obligations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double tax agreements; no domestic TRC or treaty-relief claim process exists. Dividend remittances are made gross. If a counterparty requires proof of low-tax status, the IC obtains from the VFSC a Certificate of Good Standing and a statement of tax exemption. Foreign tax authorities seeking treaty benefits must rely on their own unilateral relief provisions because Vanuatu's DTA network is limited to tax information exchange agreements (TIEAs), which provide no withholding reductions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 0% on cross-border royalties and debt interest arising from or paid to an International Company. No DTA rate differentiation is necessary. Royalty payments for the tea-salon franchise brand, brewing techniques, or ceramic salon designs may be migrated through the Vanuatu IC without domestic withholding; however, the IC must substantiate economic substance over any associated intellectual property to avoid challenge in the foreign payor jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Vanuatu VUV transfer-pricing documentation threshold applies because IC income is exempt. Nevertheless, the Economic Substance Regulations and general record-keeping rules require every IC to maintain contemporaneous documentation evidencing arm's length remuneration of intra-group transactions. Recommended minimum: full Local File style documentation where annual related-party revenue exceeds VUV 100 million (approximately USD 850,000) or where the IC owns high-value intangible property or cash-treasury assets; a Master File style overview is prudent for any group with cross-border intra-group services.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable - Vanuatu enacted the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations No. 21 of 2022 (as amended), effective 1 July 2022. Any IC carrying on a relevant activity must satisfy the management and control test in Vanuatu, maintain physical premises, employ adequate full-time staff, incur adequate local operating expenditure, and perform core income-generating activities in Vanuatu. For the Specialty Tea Salon Lounge held by the IC, two compliant structures exist: (i) the IC itself operates a genuine high-end tea salon with a Vanuatu storefront, local staff, and local POS acquiring, justifying full substance; or (ii) the IC is a pure equity-holding parent of foreign operating tea-salon entities, in which case the passive holding exemption applies with reduced substance but still requires annual ESR notification and beneficial ownership filings. A nil-activity IC may file only a notification. Asserting pure holding status while trading in tea, executing franchise agreements, or conducting treasury functions destroys the exemption and triggers strict-liability penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Misrepresentation of Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a retail specialty tea salon inside Vanuatu's domestic market under an International Company without obtaining a Business License, while falsely certifying the Certificate of Compliance and claiming ICA tax exemption for onshore-source sales; or knowingly using the IC as a vehicle to hide assets from foreign tax authorities while performing real operational activity outside Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VFSC strike-off and dissolution; referral to the Public Prosecutor for unlicensed local business activity under the Business License Act, carrying fines of up to VUV 100,000 and custodial sentence; offences of false declaration render the Tax Exemption Certificate void ab initio; the Penal Code imposes imprisonment up to 7 years for fraudulent tax-related misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: directors and beneficial owners who signed or procured the false compliance certificate are jointly and severally liable for unpaid penalties, civil restitution to the Revenue, and damages to the State; the Supreme Court may issue disqualification orders and departure prohibition orders (travel bans) pending settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a nil ESR notification while the IC in real economic terms earns holding, distribution, franchising, or service income from the tea-salon network without any local staff, premises, expenditure, or board meetings in Vanuatu, thereby abusing the passive holding exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strict-liability penalties under the Economic Substance Regulations: fines up to VUV 10 million (approximately USD 85,000) for the initial offence; continuing non-compliance accrues a daily penalty of up to VUV 250,000 per day; the VFSC may compulsorily strike off the IC and notify foreign tax authorities through TIEA channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the registered agent, and the local compliance officer are jointly liable for fines; the Supreme Court may impose a travel ban on the directors until all ESR penalties are discharged and may disqualify them from directing any Vanuatu legal entity for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain an accurate register of beneficial owners, failure to file the annual beneficial ownership return with the VFSC, refusal to cooperate with the Financial Intelligence Unit after suspicious transactions reported by the tea salon's POS and credit-card acquirer, or allowing undisclosed nominee shareholders to obscure control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines per day of default under the Companies and International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) regime; criminal prosecution for money-laundering concealment under the Proceeds of Crime Act, with penalties including imprisonment up to 5 years, forfeiture of the salon's assets, and account freezing orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto controllers face personal criminal liability, confiscation orders, and disqualification; movement across Vanuatu ports may be restricted by court order, and extradition pursuant to mutual legal assistance treaties is available for predicate money-laundering offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly continuing to accept supplier financing and customer prepayments for tea-salon franchises while insolvent; marketing the Vanuatu IC as an 'anonymous zero-tax shell' to investors without disclosing the Economic Substance and beneficial ownership obligations; or stripping assets from the salon operation to defeat creditor claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court-ordered restitution, equitable freezing injunctions, and winding-up for just and equitable grounds; fraudulent trading triggers penal fines and imprisonment up to 7 years; section 6 exemption status may be revoked and the IC dissolved with retrospective effect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered personally to contribute the entirety of the company's assets to creditors for fraudulent trading; civil recovery and disgorgement of hidden profits; imprisonment; international travel restraint; and surrender of passports pending final judgment.
